To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FDI and technological activities in the host country have contributed to its export competitiveness in the long-run.
the presence of TNCs has contributed to the export competitiveness and economic development of East Asia, and that the extent to which TNCs have contributed has varied among countries.
FDI is a major contributor to the growth in the export of high-tech goods, but it is not the only factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) how to enhance the contribution of FDI to economic growth, (ii) how technology transfer through FDI could be made more efficient, (iii) how to develop domestic technological capability and (iv) how to enhance competitiveness through technology.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the East Asian countries have been successful in attracting foreign direct investment (inward FDI) and that this has had an impact on their export competitiveness.
FDI is a necessary but not sufficient condition for export competitiveness.
FDI is not necessarily the most important factor in determining export competitiveness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the East Asian countries have been successful in attracting foreign capital, technology, and know how, and have used these inputs to enhance their competitiveness and economic growth.
FDI and domestic R&D efforts have contributed significantly to the competitiveness of East Asian economies and their growth.

the role of FDI in technology development in East Asia varies across the region.
